sentences.text: 1  ACT, PRAYING TO CALL FOR RECORDS AND ALLOW THIS APPEAL  BY MODIFYING THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 20.04.2013  PASSED BY THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, JAMKHANDI  IN LAC NO. 67/2011

AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION  AMOUNT FROM RS.2,03,700/- PER ACRE TO RS.5,00,000/- PER  ARE, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10306  MFA No. 101181 of 2023

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The claimant in L.A.C.No.67/2011 are before this Court challenging the judgment and award passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi.
The land bearing Sy.No.16/1 measuring 1 acres 18 guntas of Tunagal village, Taluk Jamkhandi, has been acquired for Hipparagi project.

Section 4(1)
notification was issued on 28.09.2006.
The Land Acquisition Officer passed an award granting compensation of Rs.72,526/- per acre treating acquired land as dry land.
2. Aggrieved by the aforementioned award of the Land Acquisition Officer, the claimant sought reference before the Reference Court.

The Reference Court awarded compensation of Rs.2,03,700/-
treating the acquired land as dry land.
3. Aggrieved by the aforementioned judgment and award, the appellant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

Sri Anil Kale, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that Survey No.16/1 measuring 1 acre 18 guntas at Tunagal village, taluk Jamkhandi which was acquired in terms of notification dated 28.09.2006 is a wet land.

He would submit that the Reference Court erred in treating the land as a dry land and he would refer to the observations made by the Land Acquisition Officer in his award to substantiate his contention that the land is wet land.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the market value determined by this Court in MFA No.102782/2020, 102783/2020 and 102784/2020 disposed of on 30.03.2021 would also apply to the present case, as in the aforementioned cases, this Court has fixed the market value in respect of the wet land acquired for Hipparagi project located in Athani taluk and Jamkhandi taluk.

6. He submits that in the aforementioned cases, the co-ordinate Bench of this Court awarded Rs.5,00,000/-

2 NC: 2023:KHC-D:10306 per acre as the compensation for the wet land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he would urge that the appellant is entitled to Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for the land acquired.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant would also submit that the beneficiary has taken a decision to award Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for all the irrigated land which are acquired for Hipparagi project, acquired between 2004 and 2007.
Thus, he would submit that the appellant is also entitled to compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the appellant's land was acquired in the year 2005.

8. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent-beneficiary is not in a position to deny the above said submission as the co-ordinate Bench of this Court has already passed an award in several cases granting Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as valuation of the irrigated land and the aforementioned judgments have not been questioned by the beneficiary and a statement is made at the Bar that the beneficiary has deposited NC: 2023:KHC-D:10306 Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for wet land which have been acquired between 2004 to 2007.
9.

The learned counsel for the appellant has also produced the Form No.C submitted by the beneficiary before the Reference Court, wherein the compensation amount is deposited at the rate of Rs.5,00,000/- per acre with all other consequential benefits in respect of lands acquired for Hipparagi project.

10. Sri K.S.Patil, learned counsel appearing for the beneficiary on other hand would contend that the Reference Court is justified in treating the land as the dry land by making reference to the record of right produced by the claimant.

He would point out to the entries in the record of right and would urge that the crop mentioned in the record of right would disclose that the land is a dry land and there is justification in the judgment and award passed by the reference Court treating the land in question as the dry land.
This Court has perused the aforementioned observations in the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
This Court has considered the rival contentions.

12. The Special Land Acquisition Officer while passing the award, has referred to the record of right pertaining to the property bearing Sy.No.16/1 referred to above and he has also referred to the joint measurement report and also made a spot inspection.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer in his award has referred to the canals found in the land and also noted that the irrigation pumps which were installed in the said property.
He has also observed that maize was grown in the said land and he has opined that the land is an irrigated land.
He has also noted that the borewell is dug in the land bearing Sy.No.16/1.
Hence, he has held that the land as irrigated land.
The Reference Court has referred to the record of right pertaining to the aforementioned property and treated the land as wet land.
It is relevant to note that the beneficiary has not led any evidence to rebut the contentions raised by the claimant land loser.
An entry in NC: 2023:KHC-D:10306 the record of right is only a prima facie proof of what might have been grown in the land acquired.

However, the entry in the Sri Tammanna S/O Pandappa Giraddi vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 8 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90170344/
3 record of right is not a conclusive proof of the nature of the land.

entities.text: Sri Tammanna S/O Pandappa Giraddi vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The presumption arising from the entries can be rebutted by leading evidence.

The claimant has produced the award by the Land Acquisition Officer which would disclose that a borewell was dug in the land and pump set was installed for the purpose of irrigation and canals were laid in the land to facilitate the flow of water.

13. This being the position, this Court is view that the finding of the Reference Court that the land is a dry land is unsustainable and same has to be set aside and the compensation has to be awarded by treating the land as wet land.
14. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent is not in a position to dispute Form No.C said to have been filed before the Reference Court.
For the above mentioned reasons, this Court is of the view that the appellant is entitled to Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for the land acquired with all statutory benefits.

16. However, it is made clear that since there was delay in filing the appeal and the delay was condoned subject to the condition that the appellant is not entitled to the interest for the delayed period in case compensation is enhanced.
The appellant is not entitled to the interest for the delayed period of 2742 days.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii.
The judgment and award dated  31.08.2009 passed by the Additional  Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi, in  L.A.C.No.67/2011 are modified.
iii. The appellant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- per acre in respect of the land acquired.
The appellant is not entitled to the interest for the delayed period of 2742 days in respect of the enhanced compensation.
v. The appellant is also entitled to  proportionate cost.
